---
title: "data ingestion & preparation"
---

## the pipeline

- source → raw snapshot → validate → transform → versioned output
- ingestion brings data from files, databases, or apis into a workflow; preparation makes it usable for the task
- keep raw inputs unchanged so you can inspect or rebuild a processed dataset

## input vocabulary

- an api is a defined interface for requesting data or invoking software; use one when a source exposes records through a service
- a raw snapshot is a preserved copy of inputs at a particular point; use it to rebuild outputs or investigate errors
- a schema specifies fields and their types; use it to detect a renamed column or an unexpected string in a numeric field
- a key identifies a logical record; use it to distinguish duplicate events from legitimate repeated observations
- batch processing handles a collection periodically; streaming handles arriving events, useful when updates need low latency

## decide before loading

- define what one row represents and the key that identifies it
- specify expected columns, types, units, time zones, and missing-value rules
- choose batch processing for periodic updates or streaming when events must be processed continuously
- record the source, extraction time, query or filters, and data version

## a tiny ingestion example

- pandas is a python library for labelled tabular data; use it here to load columns and convert their types
- csv is a text format with comma-separated fields; `StringIO` makes an in-memory text stream so the example can read csv without a separate file
- parsing converts a stored representation into a usable value, such as a timestamp string into a date-time object
- `dtype` preserves identifiers such as `001`; invalid numeric values or timestamps stop the run rather than silently becoming missing values [pandas csv parsing](https://pandas.pydata.org/docs/reference/api/pandas.read_csv.html), [numeric conversion](https://pandas.pydata.org/docs/reference/api/pandas.to_numeric.html)

```python
from io import StringIO
import pandas as pd

raw = StringIO("""record_id,event_time,amount
001,2025-02-01T10:00:00Z,12.5
002,2025-02-02T11:00:00Z,8.0
""")
df = pd.read_csv(raw, dtype={"record_id": "string"})
df["event_time"] = pd.to_datetime(df["event_time"], utc=True, errors="raise")
df["amount"] = pd.to_numeric(df["amount"], errors="raise")
if df["record_id"].isna().any() or df["record_id"].duplicated().any():
    raise ValueError("missing or duplicate record ids")
```

## make reruns safe

- design idempotent writes: processing the same input again should not create duplicate logical records
- an upsert inserts a new key or updates an existing one; use it when a repeated load contains corrected records [insert and conflict handling](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/sql-insert.html)
- a partition is a subset stored separately, such as one day’s records; replace the affected partition when rebuilding that day
- an incremental load processes changes since the previous load; a checkpoint records progress, such as the last successfully processed event id
- save a checkpoint only after the output succeeds; plan how to handle late arrivals and corrected records
- record input/output row counts and rejected rows, and publish outputs only after checks pass
- imputation fills missing values, scaling adjusts feature magnitudes, and feature selection chooses predictors; use them when the model needs those transformations
- learn these transformations from training data after splitting; do not fit them during a whole-dataset cleaning pass [leakage guidance](https://scikit-learn.org/stable/common_pitfalls.html)
